metadata.title: Warm-Up & Stretching Library
metadata.purpose: Defines warm-up and stretching protocols matched to session type. Claude uses this file to build the warm-up and cooldown blocks of every TRAIN session. Dynamic stretching always precedes training. Static stretching always follows training.
metadata.critical_rule: Dynamic warm-up BEFORE training. Static stretching AFTER training only. Static stretching before training temporarily reduces force output and increases injury risk.

instructions_for_claude.step_1: Identify session type from the program (lower body, upper body, full body, push, pull, legs, or performance)
instructions_for_claude.step_2: Select the matching warm_up_protocol from this file and place it at the start of the session
instructions_for_claude.step_3: Select the matching cooldown_and_stretching protocol and place it at the end of the session
instructions_for_claude.step_4: Apply mobility_flags from client_assessment_schema.json — add any targeted mobility work for flagged limitations
instructions_for_claude.step_5: Apply injury modifications from injury_navigation.json — replace any contraindicated warm-up movements
instructions_for_claude.step_6: For postpartum clients — use postpartum_warm_up protocol only until cleared for full programming

time_guidance.cooldown_and_stretching: 5–10 minutes — essential for recovery and flexibility
time_guidance.coaching_note: The warm-up and cooldown are not optional extras — they are part of the program. A client who skips warm-ups accumulates injury risk. A client who skips cooldowns accumulates tightness and reduces recovery quality.

purpose: Increase core temperature and blood flow to working muscles
Activate the nervous system for the demands of the session
Improve range of motion dynamically before loading
Mentally prepare the client — the warm-up is the transition from life to training
Reduce injury risk by preparing joints and connective tissue

dynamic_vs_static.dynamic: Active movements through range of motion — used in warm-up. Increases temperature, activates muscles, prepares movement patterns.
dynamic_vs_static.static: Held stretches — used in cooldown ONLY. Improves flexibility, promotes relaxation, aids recovery. Never before training.
dynamic_vs_static.kim_coaching_note: Think of the warm-up as waking the body up — and the cooldown as letting it land softly. Both matter. Both are intentional.

lower_body.focus: Hip mobility, glute activation, knee tracking, ankle dorsiflexion, posterior chain prep

sequence.name: World's Greatest Stretch
sequence.description: Lunge forward, place same-side hand on floor, rotate opposite arm to ceiling. Hold 2 seconds at top. Return and repeat.
sequence.cue: Try to show me the ceiling with your top hand. Feel the hip open and the spine rotate.
sequence.coaching_note: The single most efficient warm-up movement — covers almost every lower body limitation in one exercise. Always include.

sequence.name: Hip Circle
sequence.description: Standing, lift one knee to hip height and draw large slow circles — forward then backward.
sequence.cue: Make the circle as big as you can. Feel the hip socket moving freely.
sequence.coaching_note: Lubricates the hip joint before loading. Essential for squat and hinge patterns.

sequence.name: Glute Bridge (Activation)
sequence.description: Lie on back, feet flat, drive hips to ceiling, squeeze glutes hard at top, lower controlled.
sequence.cue: Squeeze your glutes at the top like you're trying to crack a walnut. Hold 1 second.
sequence.coaching_note: Activates glutes before compound loading — clients who skip this often compensate with lower back in squats and deadlifts.

sequence.name: Lateral Band Walk
sequence.description: Band around ankles or above knees, slight squat position, step laterally — keep tension in band throughout.
sequence.cue: Stay low. Keep your toes forward. Feel the outside of your hip working.
sequence.coaching_note: Activates glute medius — the most underworked glute muscle. Directly prevents knee cave in squats and lunges.
sequence.no_band_substitute: Bodyweight lateral squat walk — same pattern, less resistance

sequence.name: Leg Swing (Forward/Back)
sequence.description: Hold wall for balance. Swing leg forward and back in a controlled arc — increase range gradually.
sequence.cue: Let momentum build the range — don't force it. By rep 10 you should have full range.

sequence.name: Bodyweight Squat (Movement Prep)
sequence.description: Full depth bodyweight squat. Pause 1 second at bottom. Focus on depth and alignment.
sequence.cue: Sit into it. Chest up, knees tracking toes. This is the movement we're about to load — make it perfect here.
sequence.coaching_note: Final movement prep — mirrors the primary session movements at zero load.

mobility_additions.tight_hips: Add: 90/90 Hip Stretch — 60 seconds per side before sequence
mobility_additions.ankle_restriction: Add: Ankle Dorsiflexion Mobilization — 10 reps per side before squats
mobility_additions.hamstring_tightness: Add: Lying Hamstring Stretch (dynamic) — 10 leg raises per side
mobility_additions.knee_issues: Replace Lateral Band Walk with Seated Clamshell — same glute medius activation, zero knee stress

upper_body.focus: Shoulder mobility, scapular activation, thoracic rotation, rotator cuff prep, wrist and elbow readiness

sequence.name: Arm Circle
sequence.description: Stand tall, arms out to sides. Draw large slow circles forward, then reverse. Increase range gradually.
sequence.cue: Start small and let the circles get bigger. Feel the shoulder warming up.

sequence.name: Band Pull-Apart
sequence.description: Hold band at chest width with both hands, arms straight. Pull band apart until arms are wide, squeeze rear delts. Return controlled.
sequence.cue: Think about pinching a pencil between your shoulder blades at the end of every rep.
sequence.coaching_note: The most important upper body warm-up exercise — activates rear delts and scapular stabilizers that protect the shoulder on all pressing and pulling movements. Never skip.
sequence.no_band_substitute: Prone Y-T-W on floor — same activation, no equipment

sequence.name: Wall Slide
sequence.description: Stand with back against wall, arms in goal-post position. Slide arms overhead keeping contact with wall throughout. Lower back down.
sequence.cue: Keep your lower back, arms, and wrists all touching the wall the entire time. It's harder than it looks.
sequence.coaching_note: Identifies and corrects scapular dysfunction immediately. If client can't keep arms on wall — reduce range until mobility improves.

sequence.name: Thoracic Rotation (Half-Kneeling)
sequence.description: Half-kneeling position, hands behind head. Rotate upper body toward front knee. Hold 1 second. Return. Keep hips square.
sequence.cue: Your hips stay square — only your upper back rotates. Lead with your elbow to the ceiling.

sequence.name: Scapular Push-Up
sequence.description: Plank position, arms straight. Without bending elbows, let chest sink between shoulder blades (protract), then push back up (retract). Small controlled movement.
sequence.cue: Don't bend your elbows at all — this is pure shoulder blade movement. In and out.
sequence.coaching_note: Directly prepares the shoulder for pressing movements. Clients with shoulder impingement especially benefit from this.

sequence.name: External Rotation (Band or Light DB)
sequence.description: Elbow at 90 degrees at side. Rotate forearm outward away from body. Return controlled. Keep elbow pinned at side.
sequence.cue: Elbow stays glued to your side. Just the forearm rotates — like opening a door.
sequence.coaching_note: Rotator cuff activation before heavy pressing is non-negotiable for shoulder health. This is preventive medicine.

sequence.name: Wrist Circle and Wrist Mobility
sequence.sets_reps: 10 circles each direction, then 10 wrist extensions and flexions
sequence.description: Rotate wrists slowly in both directions. Then press palms together in prayer position and lower hands to stretch wrist extensors.
sequence.cue: Take your time here — wrists take a beating in pressing work.
sequence.coaching_note: Include for all upper body sessions. Essential for clients with wrist discomfort flag.

push_day_additions: Add: 1-2 light warm-up sets on primary pressing movement at 40-50% working load before working sets
pull_day_additions: Add: Dead Hang from pull-up bar — 2 x 20-30 seconds for shoulder decompression

mobility_additions.limited_shoulder: Add: Doorway Pec Stretch — 30 seconds per side before pressing work
mobility_additions.thoracic_stiffness: Add: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension — 60 seconds before sequence
mobility_additions.wrist_discomfort: Add: Extended wrist mobility sequence — fist circles, prayer stretch, reverse prayer — before any pressing

full_body.focus: Total body activation — combine lower and upper body preparation in a flowing sequence

sequence.name: March in Place
sequence.description: Walk or march in place, driving knees up to hip height. Swing arms naturally.
sequence.cue: Start easy and build your pace. Get the blood moving.
sequence.coaching_note: Simple, accessible, zero equipment. Sets the tone for the session.

sequence.name: World's Greatest Stretch
sequence.description: Lunge forward, place same-side hand on floor, rotate opposite arm to ceiling. Hold 2 seconds at top.
sequence.cue: This one movement warms up almost everything. Move slowly and intentionally.

sequence.name: Band Pull-Apart
sequence.description: Pull band from chest width to fully open. Squeeze rear delts at end range.
sequence.cue: Pinch the shoulder blades together at the end of every rep.

sequence.name: Hip Circle
sequence.description: Standing hip circles — forward and backward. Full range of motion.

sequence.name: Glute Bridge (Activation)
sequence.description: Drive hips to ceiling, 1-second squeeze at top, lower controlled.
sequence.cue: Wake those glutes up. Every rep — squeeze and hold.

sequence.name: Arm Circle + Thoracic Rotation Combo
sequence.description: 5 arm circles each direction, then 8 thoracic rotations (hands behind head, rotate upper body side to side).

sequence.name: Bodyweight Squat to Overhead Reach
sequence.description: Squat down fully, arms in front for balance. As you stand, reach both arms overhead. Lower arms on descent.
sequence.cue: Sit deep into the squat — reach tall as you stand. Full range, every rep.
sequence.coaching_note: The ideal full body warm-up finisher — integrates lower and upper body in one movement.

push_day.focus: Chest, anterior deltoid, and tricep activation. Scapular stability for pressing.

sequence.name: Band Pull-Apart
sequence.coaching_note: Always pull before you push — activates the muscles that stabilize the shoulder during pressing

sequence.name: Light Pressing Warm-Up Sets
sequence.coaching_note: Always ramp up to working weight on primary pressing movement before first working set

pull_day.focus: Lat activation, scapular retraction, bicep tendon prep, dead hang decompression

sequence.name: Dead Hang
sequence.coaching_note: Decompresses the shoulder and activates the lats before pulling. One of the most underrated warm-up movements for back training.

sequence.name: Scapular Pull-Up (or Scapular Depression on Bar)
sequence.description: Hang from bar, arms straight. Without bending elbows, depress shoulder blades (pull them down). Return.
sequence.coaching_note: Teaches the lat activation pattern before loaded pulling

performance_and_athletic.focus: CNS activation, explosive readiness, full body preparation, proprioception

sequence.name: Bodyweight Squat Jump (Sub-Maximal)
sequence.coaching_note: Sub-maximal jumps before explosive work prime the CNS without accumulating fatigue

active_recovery_and_mobility.focus: Nervous system downregulation, full body mobility, breath work

sequence.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
sequence.sets_reps: 5 slow breaths — 4 count in, hold 2, 6 count out
sequence.coaching_note: Start here. Shifts the client from stress mode to recovery mode before any movement.

sequence.name: Thread the Needle
sequence.description: On all fours, thread one arm under the body and rotate. Follow hand with eyes.

lower_body_cooldown.timing: Immediately after the final working set — while muscles are warm

sequence.name: Standing Quad Stretch
sequence.description: Stand on one leg, pull opposite foot to glute. Keep knees together, stand tall.
sequence.cue: Keep the knee pointing straight down — not flaring out to the side.

sequence.name: Standing Hip Flexor Stretch (Kneeling Lunge)
sequence.description: Kneeling lunge position. Shift hips forward gently until stretch is felt in front of back hip. Keep torso tall.
sequence.cue: Don't lean forward — stay tall. The stretch should be at the front of the back hip, not the knee.
sequence.coaching_note: Most clients who train lower body are tight through the hip flexors. This is essential every session.

sequence.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
sequence.description: Sit on floor, one leg extended. Reach toward foot with flat back. Hold.
sequence.cue: Hinge at the hip, not the waist. Keep your back flat — not rounded.

sequence.name: Pigeon Pose (or Figure Four on Back)
sequence.description: Pigeon: front shin parallel, back leg long behind. Fold forward gently. Figure Four (easier): lie on back, cross ankle over opposite knee, pull thigh toward chest.
sequence.cue: Breathe into the tightest part of the stretch. Let it release with each exhale.
sequence.coaching_note: The most important lower body cooldown stretch. Glutes tighten significantly during heavy lower body work — always include.

sequence.name: Calf Stretch (Wall)
sequence.description: Hands on wall, one foot forward, one back. Press back heel into floor. Keep back leg straight for gastrocnemius, slight knee bend for soleus.

sequence.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
sequence.description: Lie on back, loop band or towel around foot. Straighten leg toward ceiling gently. Keep opposite leg flat.
sequence.coaching_note: Use after deadlift or RDL days especially — hammers right into the belly of the hamstring.

sequence.name: Child's Pose
sequence.description: Kneel and sit back on heels, reach arms long in front, forehead to floor.
sequence.cue: Let everything go. Breathe slowly. The work is done.
sequence.coaching_note: Closes the session with a moment of intentional rest. Aligns with Kim's mind-body philosophy.

sequence.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
sequence.description: Pull one arm across the body at shoulder height. Use opposite hand to gently increase stretch. Keep shoulder down.

sequence.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
sequence.description: Stand in doorway, arm at 90 degrees on frame. Gently rotate body away until stretch is felt across chest. Hold.
sequence.cue: Don't force it — gentle rotation. You should feel this across your chest, not in your shoulder joint.
sequence.coaching_note: Most pressing-dominant clients are tight through the pec. Essential after push days.

sequence.name: Overhead Tricep Stretch
sequence.description: Raise one arm overhead, bend elbow, reach hand down back. Use opposite hand to gently push elbow back.

sequence.name: Bicep Wall Stretch
sequence.description: Place palm flat on wall at shoulder height, fingers pointing down or back. Gently rotate body away.
sequence.coaching_note: Include after any pulling-heavy session — biceps shorten significantly during curl and row work.

sequence.name: Neck Side Stretch
sequence.description: Gently tilt ear toward shoulder. Hold with light hand pressure. Never force.
sequence.cue: No pulling — just weight of the hand. This is gentle.

sequence.name: Sleeper Stretch
sequence.description: Lie on side on floor with arm at 90 degrees. Use opposite hand to gently press wrist toward floor. Keep shoulder pinned.
sequence.coaching_note: Highly effective for shoulder health after heavy pressing. Include after push days for any client with shoulder tightness.

sequence.name: Thread the Needle
sequence.description: On all fours, slide one arm under body and rest on that shoulder. Other arm reaches to ceiling optionally.
sequence.cue: Let gravity do the work. Breathe and release.

sequence.name: Child's Pose
sequence.cue: Let everything settle. The work is done. Breathe slowly.

performance_cooldown.note: Athletes accumulate more systemic fatigue — longer cooldown is warranted

sequence.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
sequence.coaching_note: Close every performance session with intentional breathing — brings the nervous system down from fight-or-flight

lower_back.note: Keep all movements gentle and unloaded. Build core stability before any loading.

knee.note: Activate VMO and glute medius before any knee-loaded movement.

shoulder.note: Rotator cuff activation must precede any pressing or pulling.

postpartum.note: Reference injury_navigation.json postpartum protocol for phase-appropriate warm-up.

coaching_language_for_warm_up.opening: Before we get into the work — let's prepare the body. This isn't just a formality. The warm-up is where we wake up and arrive.
coaching_language_for_warm_up.during: Notice how your body is feeling right now. The warm-up is information — tight hips, stiff shoulders, low energy. We adjust from here.
coaching_language_for_warm_up.closing_warm_up: Your body is ready. Let's train.
coaching_language_for_warm_up.opening_cooldown: You did the work. Now let's let the body land. This is where recovery begins.
coaching_language_for_warm_up.during_cooldown: Breathe into the stretch. Each exhale — release a little more. The work is done. This is the reward.
coaching_language_for_warm_up.closing_cooldown: Session complete. Every rep today was a choice to show up for yourself. That matters.
